metadata.title: GAO Finds DOGE $215B Savings Claims Fabricated; 96% of Grants Unverifiable

existing_copy_for_context_only.short: GAO Finds DOGE $215B Savings Claims Fabricated; 96% of Grants Unverifiable
existing_copy_for_context_only.medium: A Government Accountability Office review of DOGE’s “Wall of Receipts” found that many reported savings could not be verified from the documentation provided. The supplied figures include grant claims with no supporting methodology and contract terminations with no action taken. The findings concern the transparency and calculation of savings claims, not a verified total of realized federal savings.
existing_copy_for_context_only.long: On August 6, 2026, the Government Accountability Office released a comprehensive audit of DOGE's Wall of Receipts savings claims. Of 13,476 contracts DOGE claimed to have terminated, no termination action was actually taken on 2,503 of them. In one case, DOGE continued claiming $1.7 billion in savings from a Defense Health Agency IT contract even after Pentagon officials got DOGE to agree the contract should remain — and no action was taken. DOGE had claimed $113 million in lease savings, but GAO found the actual figure was $53.5 million; 108 of 264 leases claimed as DOGE cuts were already in the termination process before DOGE existed, representing $15.3 million in misappropriated credit. For grant savings, DOGE claimed $49.2 billion but GAO could not verify 96.2 percent of it — approximately $47.32 billion — because DOGE provided no methodology or supporting data. The linked New York Times article concerns Trump’s indictment, not Bannon’s subpoena case.

Judge Carl Nichols sentenced him to four months in prison and a $6,500 fine. Bannon remained free while appealing the conviction, and Donald Trump pardoned him after returning to the White House in January 2025. The conviction followed the committee’s effort to obtain evidence and testimony from people connected to Trump’s efforts to overturn the 2020 election.
